objective: Extend SQLolla's verified-by-testing M1 relational foundation toward single-table CRUD and sequential transactions, while retaining the full pinned SQLeanParser typed-AST surface as the MVP goal.
implementation_authorization: User authorized expansion to all 276 corpus records with explicit application contexts and expected PostgreSQL errors; unsupported and resource refusals are not coverage.

baseline.preserve: Re-run current canonical M0/M1 gates unchanged. These counts describe the baseline and are not M2 evidence.

industrial_census.interpretation: Syntax/export census only. Diagnostics report the first blocker, overlap across capabilities, and cannot be added to predict future execution coverage.
industrial_census.acquisition: Keep original corpus hashes, source URLs, commits and declared transformations. New actual-PG runs must retain exact SQL and label synthetic catalog/data/session context; never relabel an extracted or adapted case as a complete production workload.

industrial_runtime.catalog_kind: explicit synthetic test catalogs; no production-DDL claim
industrial_runtime.coverage: 7 BenchBase queries and 1 Temporal query; additional source/context coverage remains an M2 gate

first_deliverable.order: Lean contracts before any M2 implementation slice

modules.Outcome: SQLSTATE/phase and distinct column/constraint diagnostics, completed versus refused attempts, atomic candidate rejection, CHECK/NOT NULL and unique-NULL distinctions.
modules.Scalar: Mathematical Int32 arithmetic with checked result range, zero division and signed division overflow/truncation.
modules.Crud: Occurrence identity, UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT and nontarget table frames, old-row simultaneous assignment example.
modules.Transaction: Structured sequential execution, original abort cause, subsequent 25P02, distinct logical termination versus COMMIT/ROLLBACK command tags, commit-time rejection and retained observations.
modules.Coverage: Reference/model admission and bad-behavior agreement; separate outcome soundness/completeness; transfer of all inherited bounded-claim obligations; a countermodel to input coverage alone.
modules.Extensions: COUNT/SUM NULL and duplicate behavior, empty global aggregate, ordered ties and different LIMIT pages.
modules.Witnesses: Kernel-checked tenant mutation, stock rejection/rollback and retained RETURNING examples.

first_deliverable.verification: Run pwsh -File contracts/m2/verify.ps1; retain verification.json only after a successful build and module-owned transitive trust audit.
first_deliverable.trust: No proof placeholders, custom or unapproved assumptions, privileged shortcuts or native proof evaluation. Only inherited propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound foundations are allowed. Audit includes generated/private declarations by owner module.
first_deliverable.proof_scope: Abstract contracts, selected executable mathematical operations and conditional lemmas. There is no proven PostgreSQL semantics, parser preservation, Rust refinement or Alloy encoding equivalence.
open_obligations: Reference execution relation and finite domain completeness must be supplied for each admitted feature.
The generic final-state validator does not establish PostgreSQL's constraint enforcement order.
The scalar functions consume already available operands; planner folding and evaluation order are not implemented.
Aggregate counts/sums are mathematical. PostgreSQL bigint/numeric result types and overflow remain explicit implementation obligations.
AllowedOrder is an abstract ordering contract; the concrete comparator, collation, null placement and all permitted tie outcomes remain to be instantiated.

compatibility_contract.deterministic_boundary: SQLeanParser typed AST -> versioned Rust binding -> typed RA/effect IR -> deterministic Alloy source; AI never supplies executable semantics or a safety verdict.
compatibility_contract.m1: Existing pure relational nodes, duplicate/NULL behavior, context fingerprints, strict rejection of unknown fields, timeouts, complete occurrence capacities and replay labels remain regression invariants.
compatibility_contract.extension_protocol: Introduce explicit statement/effect/error/ordered-result variants; version incompatible envelopes. Keep M1 compatibility intentional, tested and documented rather than silently reinterpreting its schema.
compatibility_contract.transaction_input: Use an explicit sequential transaction envelope with an ordered list of individually parsed SQL statements and a requested commit/rollback action. Do not claim SQLeanParser parses BEGIN/COMMIT until its actual AST supports them.
compatibility_contract.architecture: Rust owns types, arithmetic, state transitions, evaluation, bounds and encoding. Java 17 remains an isolated Alloy API bridge. Lean is a specification/trust gate.
compatibility_contract.style: Each authored method/declaration is at most 30 physical lines; purpose documentation and Rustdoc/Javadoc accompany implementation. Pure transformations return typed errors; I/O remains at controlled process boundaries.
compatibility_contract.deployment: M2 stays offline and local during semantic promotion. Preserve Windows behavior and prepare native Linux/macOS CI; do not claim unexecuted platforms or sqlolla.us deployment are validated.

workstreams.deliverable: Freeze the contracts, capability matrix, source inventory and baseline regression evidence.
acceptance: Independent review of every conditional guarantee and missing reference semantics.
Kernel/source/style audit passes; inherited M0 source hashes are unchanged.
Every proposed feature lists parse/export/bind/evaluate/encode/replay/PG/adversarial stages separately.

workstreams.deliverable: Admit required Int32 arithmetic, comparisons and explicit error outcomes for business updates.
scope: Checked + and -; add division only with zero and MIN/-1 branches.
Typed NULL propagation after operand evaluation; cast/input and planning failures remain distinct.
Pure CASE/COALESCE or other short-circuit constructs need dedicated PostgreSQL evaluation obligations before admission.
acceptance: Actual-PG signed range, zero, NULL and parameter cases.
No host wrapping or Alloy finite-integer wrapping is used as SQL arithmetic.
Reference error branches survive into the failure query; planner/eager evaluation cases are refused until justified.

workstreams.deliverable: Single-target INSERT VALUES/SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE with explicit before/after frames, affected counts and RETURNING, followed by sequential commit/abort/rollback.
scope: Start with ordinary tables, explicit known schema and total admitted assignments; update each selected occurrence from the old row.
DELETE RETURNING uses deleted values; INSERT/UPDATE RETURNING uses the appropriate new values.
Single-table statements may compose across tables inside one sequential transaction; nontarget tables remain framed.
No need to finish all S3/S4 capabilities before starting this workstream.
acceptance: Failed statement cannot publish a partial candidate; later statements do not resume mutation after failure.
Prior client-visible results, and any admitted streaming emission before an error, remain observable despite rollback.
A zero-row mutation succeeds with affected count zero; unchanged matched UPDATE rows still count.
All admitted constructors preserve duplicates and exact occurrence lineage without turning internal occurrence IDs into SQL keys.

workstreams.deliverable: Catalog-declared NOT NULL, pure row CHECK, and a carefully admitted UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY profile; extend foreign keys and deferred timing through explicit subsequent slices.
scope: Validate prestate admissibility separately from candidate execution.
CHECK UNKNOWN passes; NOT NULL is independent; default UNIQUE and NULLS NOT DISTINCT differ.
Immediate uniqueness needs intermediate enforcement semantics: a valid final key permutation can still fail. Do not approve key-changing multirow UPDATE from a final-state check alone.
Commit validator is explicit even while deferred constraints are refused by the initial executable profile.
acceptance: Violations produce named SQLSTATE outcomes; no constraint is merely asserted as a poststate fact.
Multi-constraint failures require exact admitted timing or a clearly labeled conservative error abstraction.
Self/intra-batch unique collisions, unchanged duplicates, key swaps and deferred failures have actual-PG fixtures.
Defaults, identity/sequence, generated columns, triggers, RLS, FK actions, inheritance/partitioning and unsupported metadata fail closed until their effects are modeled.

workstreams.deliverable: High-corpus-impact ORDER BY/LIMIT/OFFSET and selected COUNT/SUM/MIN/MAX grouping/derived compositions in parallel with CRUD where staffing permits.
scope: Separate ordered results from bags; encode every permitted tie outcome or require a proven unique ordering key for the admitted pagination profile.
Pin ASC/DESC, NULL placement, exact text/collation profile, parameterized LIMIT/OFFSET errors and empty/global/grouped results.
Add bigint output typing for COUNT and SUM(integer) before implementation; AVG/numeric needs its own type slice.
Aggregate DISTINCT/FILTER, HAVING, derived results and CTE composition are capability increments, not syntactic passthrough.
acceptance: Compare ordered results as sequences and unordered results as bags.
Enumerate tie cases independently; one observed PostgreSQL plan is not evidence that other allowed outcomes do not exist.
Grouped empty input versus global empty aggregation, NULL grouping keys, duplicate occurrences and aggregate overflow are tested.
Track exact unchanged industrial SQL that advances beyond its first ORDER BY blocker.

workstreams.deliverable: Continue the complete typed-AST MVP through subqueries/correlation, USING/NATURAL, functions/types, upsert/defaults/catalog changes and a separately specified concurrency model.
workstreams.rule: S1..S6 are workstream labels, not a mandatory serial pipeline. Dependencies follow semantic prerequisites. Any still-refused family remains in the MVP ledger with a concrete next obligation.
deferred_guarantees: No lost-update, write-skew, isolation-level or locking guarantees follow from the sequential M2 model.
No arbitrary Alloy-to-SQL inverse: only recognized typed IR/effect patterns can be pretty-printed and round-trip checked.
Full triggers/RLS/UDF behavior cannot be replaced by uninterpreted functions under a database-security claim.

modeled_outcomes: Statement SQL errors and original cause

property_examples.name: tenant_write_scope
property_examples.bad: A row outside the authorized tenant changes at an admitted observation/state boundary.

property_examples.name: tenant_disclosure
property_examples.bad: An output event exposes unauthorized tenant data, even when the transaction later aborts.

property_examples.name: stock_nonnegative
property_examples.bad: A specifically chosen committed or intermediate observation contains negative stock; the property must name which boundary matters.

property_examples.name: unexpected_rejection
property_examples.bad: A policy requiring success encounters a modeled SQL error; expected validation rejection is not automatically a security flaw.

failure_and_scope_policy.coverage_equation: forall admitted input and every reference outcome: reference_exec(input,outcome) -> modeled_exec(input,outcome); witness soundness requires the reverse direction on the admitted domain.
no_counterexample_gate: Complete finite scopes and arithmetic/result domains
bounds: Count every intermediate state/row occurrence, insert capacity, affected/returning occurrence and ordered permutation branch.
Cover arithmetic result values and error branches, not just prestate input literals; compute closed finite result domains or refuse.
Cardinality SAT bitwidth is independent of SQL Int32/Int64 width; forbid overflow at either layer.
Resource limits, unsupported effects, incomplete context, timeout and solver errors yield refusal/inconclusive, never a safety label.
failure_and_scope_policy.abstraction_rule: A conservative overapproximation may support an appropriately qualified absence claim with completeness evidence, but SAT then yields a candidate until reference replay validates it. Underapproximation cannot justify UNSAT.
failure_and_scope_policy.observations: Buffered atomic is a specific constructor, not a universal client/server behavior guarantee. The general failed-statement outcome retains already exposed rows; model or explicitly exclude network/driver streaming profiles.
failure_and_scope_policy.result_integrity: Evidence fingerprints bind complete SQL, parameters, catalog/constraints, session and transaction settings, bounds/domain, property, tool versions and all before/after/error/observation data. A replay bundle must include all required catalog tables and context.

semantic_matrix: INSERT duplicates/empty source/default omission; UPDATE no matches/same value/old-row column swap; DELETE TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN.
Multirow candidate expression failure rolls back all rows; a later statement failure rolls back earlier writes.
RETURNING old/new values, prior successful observations and admitted same-statement emission before error.
NOT NULL versus CHECK UNKNOWN; unique NULL modes; multirow key swaps; commit-time rejection.
Int32 MIN/MAX, signed division/truncation, divide by zero, NULL operands, constant folding and error phase.
AND/OR/CASE and aggregate expressions with error-producing branches; do not assume lexical short-circuiting.
GROUP BY empty/global distinction, NULL groups, duplicate aggregates, HAVING and COUNT/SUM output types.
Ordering ties, NULL placement, LIMIT/OFFSET zero/NULL/negative/out of range and composition with DISTINCT.
Tenant predicate omission, tenant changes in assignments, shared stock depletion and rollback disclosure.
validation.oracle: Extend the actual PostgreSQL 16 harness to capture prestate, typed results, affected counts, SQLSTATE plus separate column/constraint/phase diagnostics, command completion tags, logical transaction termination, observations and final committed state. COMMIT after an already failed transaction can complete with ROLLBACK; do not invent a new SQL error. Reset schema and state per case; record role, search_path, collation, timezone, constraints and driver buffering mode.
validation.symbolic: Independently enumerate tiny input bags, parameter domains, statement sequences and permitted outcome choices. Compare Rust and decoded Alloy outcomes with the reference set, not merely SAT witness existence.
validation.industrial: Rerun all 276 records at every stage and retain denominators, unchanged SQL hashes and per-stage first failures. Separate corpus syntax/export progress from cases actually executed with an adequate catalog and from verified transaction properties.
validation.industrial_promotion: Select genuine multi-statement business procedures only when grouping, parameter flow and catalog metadata are known; record synthetic scaffolding explicitly. Never construct invented transaction boundaries and label them original industrial transactions.
mutations: Treat UNIQUE NULL as equal by default
validation.regression: Current M0 trust gate and all M1 parser/Rust/PG/symbolic/negative/mutant/style/capacity gates remain mandatory; M2 adds tests rather than replacing their meaning.
validation.promotion: Freeze sources, independently review semantics and evidence, run final gates once, update the canonical capability ledger, and remove failed temporary probes/duplicate reports before proposing any production promotion.

delegation.handoff: Kernel-checked definitions, visible assumptions and finite counterexamples; cannot certify implementation by declaration alone.

delegation.owns: Complete typed-AST field preservation, catalog/parameter/error binding and explicit capability refusals
delegation.handoff: Versioned protocol changes and supported/unsupported constructor census; no handwritten SQL parser.

delegation.owns: Pure effect interpreter, bounds, deterministic state/observation encoding and witness reconstruction
delegation.handoff: Per-operator semantic correspondence tests and exact capacity accounting.

delegation.owns: Independent actual-PG oracle, unchanged industrial SQL replays, finite exhaustive outcome checks and mutants
delegation.handoff: Concrete divergences, coverage gaps and reproducible complete replay bundles.

delegation.owns: Cross-agent contract reconciliation, provenance, platform boundaries, source freeze and promotion decision
delegation.handoff: Review closed on exact source hashes; unresolved gaps remain explicit.

ranked_review_risks.risk: A bad/error outcome is eliminated by assuming constraints or success.
ranked_review_risks.review: Separate input assumptions from transition errors; use complete-outcome countermodel and targeted mutants.

ranked_review_risks.risk: Final-state-only UNIQUE checks or lexical expression order invent PostgreSQL behavior.
ranked_review_risks.review: Require actual enforcement timing and reference outcome coverage; refuse unresolved combinations.

ranked_review_risks.risk: Intermediate scope/result-domain truncation creates false UNSAT.
ranked_review_risks.review: Independent cardinality/state/value closure bounds; overflow and minimum-insufficient-scope mutants.

ranked_review_risks.risk: Rollback is incorrectly presented as erasing disclosed rows.
ranked_review_risks.review: Preserve statement and transaction observations, including admitted streaming emissions.

ranked_review_risks.risk: Ordered pagination drops ties or aggregation narrows the output type.
ranked_review_risks.review: All-order outcomes, comparator/context profile and PostgreSQL result-type fixtures.

ranked_review_risks.risk: Industrial syntax progress is marketed as transaction verification.
ranked_review_risks.review: Publish per-stage denominators and complete known context; label synthetic scaffolding.

ranked_review_risks.risk: M2 accidentally changes M1 or blocks CRUD behind unrelated advanced syntax.
ranked_review_risks.review: Isolated drafts, unchanged regression gates and prerequisite-based parallel workstreams.

m3_boundary.status: Separate feasibility workstream; not a prerequisite or semantic oracle for M2.
m3_boundary.observed_by_integrator: Small qualitative M3 experiments covered explanation reference closure, typed-RA candidates checked by the deterministic binder and PG, and blind witness predictions. These do not establish general AI reliability.
m3_boundary.providers: BYOT adapters may retain OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini-compatible interfaces, but all authorized production AI flows are pinned to exact gpt-6.1-sol on a verified endpoint. No silent fallback or substitute model; credentials remain ephemeral and live compatibility must be tested.
m3_boundary.contract: AI may propose typed edits and explain immutable evidence with valid references. The deterministic compiler and verifier accept/reject changes; AI text cannot create a bounded claim or alter constraints.
m3_boundary.ui: Use AlloyStudio-like instance exploration only with separate full/transport/view completeness and explicit error/commit/rollback/observation timelines.

references.supports: Stable SQLSTATE comparison and initial error-family mapping.
Old-row assignment input, updated-row RETURNING and affected-row counts.
Immediate versus deferred enforcement, including immediate nondeferrable uniqueness.
Expression evaluation and planner/aggregate ordering subtleties.
Aggregate NULL behavior and PostgreSQL output types.
Separate column-name and constraint-name diagnostic fields.

review_closures.change: Failure now has separate optional columnName and constraintName fields; requireNonNull populates only columnName, with a checked theorem.
review_closures.evidence: Integrator independently ran PostgreSQL 16.16 GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS after INSERT NULL into x int NOT NULL: SQLSTATE 23502, column x, empty constraint field. Temporary probe cluster removed.
review_closures.finding: NOT NULL error incorrectly stored column identity in constraintName.

review_closures.change: Finished records EndProtocol separately from EndReason. failed_commit_protocol proves COMMIT after a failed transaction yields a ROLLBACK completion tag while retaining the original cause.
review_closures.evidence: Independently executed PostgreSQL16.16 BEGIN; SELECT1/0; COMMIT with ON_ERROR_STOP=0. Command tags were BEGIN then ROLLBACK; SQL failure remained on stderr; ephemeral cluster removed. Protocol tags remain separate mandatory fields in the planned transaction oracle.
review_closures.finding: Logical abort could be mistaken for a COMMIT protocol error.

snapshot.meaning: Historical full-run backlog. Later focused passes are component evidence only; refresh contexts and replay all 276 records before changing this count. Historical first-refusal codes are not an exhaustive dependency inventory.

formalization_first.before_new_code: Extend kernel-checked contracts for function resolution/coercion, scalar effect composition, CTE demand, regex and tuple-version observations before their Rust integration. Existing abstract contracts do not prove PostgreSQL equivalence or Rust refinement.
formalization_first.trust: No sorry, sorryAx, custom/unapproved axioms, unsafe proof shortcuts or native_decide; audit transitive declarations. Only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are allowed foundations.

remaining_corpus_patterns.grouping_rule: Each record appears in exactly one primary scheduling group. Semantic dependencies overlap; closing one group does not automatically credit its records. Names are exact unique final segments of ledger IDs; population and source SQL remain in the ledger.

groups.pattern: Scalar-looking calls change sequence, notification, lock or backend state; some sit inside lazy expressions and materialized CTEs.
Lock a selected prefix or derived relation, mutate matching rows, expose RETURNING and same-snapshot fallback rows.
Sibling UNNEST expressions form aligned rows feeding aggregation, joins, catalog lookup or bulk mutations.
groups.caution: jobSetStateIfRunningMany has no explicit row-lock clause. Its dependencies are aligned expansion, joined mutation, correlated fallback, UNION ALL and ordering.

groups.pattern: Ordinary writes require complete standalone/partial unique-index metadata, defaults and declared immutable function bodies.
groups.caution: The old ledger refused incomplete write metadata. This is not evidence that each query needs a new DML operator; default sequence evaluation is additionally required for jobInsertFull.

groups.pattern: JSONB key existence and conditional concatenation over typed NULL-aware values.
groups.caution: jobUpdate's old mismatch arose from missing JSONB concatenation returning 42883 with an empty error schema; do not invent an output-label patch from that historical symptom.

groups.pattern: Locked and paginated candidates are partitioned/ranked, checked against uniqueness policy and updated through CTEs.
Catalog joins and string slicing followed by PostgreSQL regex matching, here ^_cc(new|old)[0-9]*$.

proposed_types.Branch<T>: Typed value/outcome plus branch-local database, catalog, held ownership, pending notifications, sequence state and ordered external-event trace.
proposed_types.OutcomeSet<T>: All admitted bounded alternatives, with explicit completeness and resource status; never silently truncate to one convenient execution.
proposed_types.ScalarObservation: Typed Cell plus branch state/events, including distinct non-NULL void and SQL NULL(void).
proposed_types.Demand: All | Prefix(offset, limit) | Exists, with planning-time observations separate from execution-time consumption.
proposed_types.WithFrame: Original statement snapshot, materialized CTE relation slots, pending write deltas, dependency/demand information and branch-local effects.

rules: Admission refusal and resource exhaustion remain distinct from modeled PostgreSQL SQLSTATE outcomes.
Each alternative owns its state; no shared mutable Runtime effect log. Pass inherited state into child execution before it runs: appending prior effects afterward is insufficient for nextval.
Merge lock ownership by identity/strength; retain ordered event multiplicity. A materialized CTE reference must not append its evaluation events again.
CASE/COALESCE preserve selected-branch demand; Boolean evaluation follows the admitted PostgreSQL planning/evaluation profile, not an invented universal left-to-right rule.

On statement-savepoint rollback, restore pre-existing transactional ownership/notification state and table state; retain actual nontransactional sequence allocations. Commit delivery is a separate step.
Pure operators preserve already-produced effects even when their output is empty; demand analysis determines which upstream operations actually ran.

Demand transfer is operator-specific: Prefix/Exists cannot pass blindly through sorting, aggregation/windows, DISTINCT or materialization. Validate each transfer and preserve planning-time errors independently of row demand.
Backend signaling has its own irreversible observation semantics and must not be filtered through a rollback function that currently retains only sequence events.
shared_execution_contract.existing_foundation: crates/sqlolla-core/src/execution/rel_effects.rs; extend its typed composition rather than add a second evaluator or query-name handlers.

branch_effects.design: Shared execution contract above; pure calls retain a fast path, effectful calls return explicit branch observations.
branch_effects.state: Branch-local scalar and relational effects, lazy CASE/COALESCE, per-proposal defaults, retained nontransactional errors and CTE inherited prefixes are implemented. Unsupported competing tuple interleavings and effectful scalar subqueries remain explicit refusals.

typed_builtins.reuse: scalar/arrays.rs, array_functions.rs, json_functions.rs, json_update.rs and comparison.rs
typed_builtins.remaining: Remaining overload/coercion and locale semantics stay explicit capability work. Known builtin identities use the pinned inventory; declared SQL function bodies, NULL policies and volatility use shared metadata. See capabilities.json for the concrete adversarial signature backlog.
typed_builtins.evidence: Canonical actual-PG results: validation/results/{collections,comparability,sql_functions,xid-scalars}.json; read current hashes and failures rather than historical per-pass counts.

set_expansion.invariants: Longest sibling length, typed NULL padding, duplicate preservation and per-input-row element order; enumerate permitted input-row orders before LIMIT. Nested scalar wrappers consume expanded cells, not independently rerun UNNEST.
set_expansion.evidence: 32 focused cases and 47 actual-PG executions passed; bulk-write composition still needs integrated replay.

write_rules.reuse: unique_index.rs, execution/index_arbiter.rs, expression/sql_function.rs and existing CRUD/constraints modules
write_rules.invariants: Standalone indexes differ from named constraints; partial predicates require a sound implication rule and the registry's immutable-expression gate. Preserve old-row simultaneous assignments, joined-source alternatives, SQLSTATE, nontarget frames and RETURNING lineage. Defaults use the same lazy scalar evaluator. Multiple simultaneously violated constraints require authentic enforcement ordering or an explicit diagnostic-ambiguity refusal.
write_rules.evidence: Actual PostgreSQL uniqueness-order, immutable partial-index and SQL-function resolution probes are maintained in unique_indexes.json and sql_functions.json. Catalog contexts retain real index enforcement order and invalidate stale comparison evidence.

cte_flow.reuse: execution/with_statement.rs, cte_schedule.rs, cte_demand.rs, cte_consumption.rs and cte_lineage/{closure,trace,mutation}.rs
cte_flow.invariants: Original base-table reads, materialized RETURNING relations and pending writes remain separate. Shared read CTEs execute according to demand; data-modifying CTEs obey their completion semantics. Reusing a CTE cannot duplicate a sequence allocation or notification. Textual CTE order is not a universal execution order: enumerate admitted dependency-consistent schedules for independent writes/effects, or refuse noncommuting cases until covered.
cte_flow.remaining: General streaming consumers, competing multirow effects, ambiguous source matches, error-prefix consumption and correlated membership lineage require further explicit semantics. Successful per-branch certificates preserve occurrence identity and every alternative; refusals never contribute coverage.

row_locks.invariants: Consumed/locked rows differ from returned rows. Apply SKIP LOCKED, OFFSET and LIMIT at their correct stages; preserve stable occurrence identity, including duplicates. Planning-time relation locks are separate from row acquisition.
row_locks.evidence: Actual PostgreSQL lock ownership probes: locking.json, locking_join.json, cte-locks.json and lock_initialization.json. Stored-view lock inheritance, unspecified waits and ambiguous origins remain refused.

sequences.invariants: is_called, increment, bounds, cycle, permission, identity and cache ownership are explicit. Allocation is lazy and survives a later failed write/rollback. Each alternative starts from its own prior state.
sequences.state: Lean-checked allocation contracts and SQL execution are integrated under exclusive cache-one snapshots. Sequence state survives statement failure/rollback; expression order and CTE producer/default competition have actual-PG regressions in sequence-effects.json.

session_effects.invariants: Notification invocation, queue and delivered events differ; duplicate delivery folding occurs at commit and rollback delivers none. Advisory keys retain bigint/int-pair namespace and ownership. Backend signal acceptance is distinct from confirmed termination.
session_effects.state: SessionEffects and BackendSignals contracts, pure runtime transitions and actual PG suites are integrated. Notifications retain invocation order but fold identical commit deliveries; rollback discards pending delivery. Stable owned backend targets test accepted signal requests separately from observed eventual exit; no-target corpus evidence is only the independently proved no-call branch.
session_effects.testing: Use disposable owned PostgreSQL workers for positive backend scenarios; never terminate user/server application sessions.

windows.invariants: Shared slots for repeated calls, typed partition keys and complete permitted tie alternatives; preserve input effects through ranking and later mutation.
windows.evidence: Focused windows.json plus composed jobSchedule fixtures in the full industrial ledger; all permitted tie alternatives remain bounded and explicit.

regex.design: A checked bounded regex IR for admitted PostgreSQL anchors, alternation, groups, classes and repetition; no query-name or literal-pattern special case and no assumed Rust-regex equivalence.
regex.remaining: The admitted bounded regex subset is implemented and differentially tested in regex-subset.json. General ARE extensions, backreferences and locale-sensitive behavior remain refused; bounds never silently truncate matching.

system_columns.invariants: xmax is tuple-version metadata, not an upsert Boolean. Execution requires checked exclusive top-level transaction/header context; version events retain row lineage, old-header lock state and aborted residuals.
system_columns.remaining: INSERT/ON CONFLICT RETURNING is integrated with actual PG tuple and unchanged River nonempty-array tests. Ordinary UPDATE/DELETE tuple context, MultiXact, external writers, subtransactions and savepoints remain explicit boundaries.

relation_initialization.invariants: Capture physical relation opening before unused/dead-query pruning; initialize once before row demand. Never infer tuple locking from relation opening; planner failures and rollback retain their distinct timing.

consumer_lineage.invariants: Trace the original effectful query once; replay only pure materialized inputs under the same branch prefix. Preserve distinct duplicate occurrences, reject uncertified error alternatives, require event closure and do not infer empty demand from eager evaluation.

delivery_order: Complete independent reviews and preserve kernel/source trust gates before semantic edits.
Finish typed-builtin gaps and comparability checks; refresh index/function contexts together and invalidate stale request-dependent coverage.
Unify lazy scalar and CTE effect composition; integrate lock-demand paths, then sequence and transactional session effects.
Implement the independent regex leaf in parallel; start bounded system-column/backend observation contracts early because these are the highest semantic risks.
Integrate composite bulk/window queries using shared modules; prohibit dispatch by corpus ID or SQL fingerprint.
Rebuild once for a coordinated validation wave, rerun focused probes and all 276 records with both fixtures, then re-run M0/M1 gates and exact Alloy witness checks.
adversarial_acceptance: Unequal/empty/NULL arrays, lower bounds and duplicate IDs; arrays cannot become a Cartesian product or lose repeated rows.
Empty-input planning errors, lazy unreachable calls, JSON versus JSONB equality and builtin-specific NULL rules.
CTE referenced twice, unused read CTE, data-modifying CTE completion, constant-false consumers and LIMIT 0; separate relation locks from row locks.
Independent writable CTEs with noncommuting effects cannot inherit lexical source order as execution semantics; test all admitted schedules and demand barriers through sort/group/window/DISTINCT.
Sequence allocations followed by uniqueness error, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and transaction rollback; do not refund allocations.
Partial-index UNKNOWN predicate, standalone index versus constraint name, schema/function permission and argument identity.
Notification duplicate invocations versus delivered messages, multibyte limits, NULL channel/payload, savepoint and transaction rollback.
Competing advisory/row ownership, unresolved blocking schedules and effectful binary evaluation order cannot be erased or guessed.
Regex invalid patterns, newline/collation boundaries and resource limits; resource refusal never counts as matching SQL behavior.
xmax on visible locked/updated/aborted tuple versions; backend signal acceptance versus observed process termination.
Compare schema, output multiplicity/order, exact expected errors, affected counts, complete database/catalog frames and independently observed effects.
Alloy table roundtrip retains its finite-evaluator assurance label; it is not an independent proof of SQL semantics. Keep assumption SAT runs separate from property checks.
276/276 means the pinned corpus under declared contexts, not all production PostgreSQL. Add positive fixtures for newly modeled effects instead of earning feature claims only from empty inputs.

open_review_findings.observation: Historical confirmed finding: With public.abs(integer) returning 999 and implicit pg_catalog precedence, SELECT abs(1) returns 1 in PostgreSQL but 999 in CLI 289de0f8. Declared f(integer) called with text/bigint also exposes wrong SQLSTATE/refusal classification.
open_review_findings.resolution: Shared qualified function/signature resolver, checked call-coercion rules and persistent actual-PG regressions before promotion.

open_review_findings.observation: Historical confirmed finding: Partial-index binding currently checks Boolean type without a shared immutable-expression gate.
open_review_findings.resolution: Registry-backed volatility admission before accepting index metadata.

setup_sql: CREATE TABLE t(a integer UNIQUE, b integer)
ALTER TABLE t ADD PRIMARY KEY(b)
open_review_findings.observation: Historical confirmed finding: PostgreSQL16 reports 23505/t_a_key; CLI 289de0f8 reports 23505/t_pkey. Creating both constraints in one CREATE can hide this ordering defect.
open_review_findings.resolution: Preserve authentic uniqueness enforcement identity/order or refuse ambiguous diagnostics until the admitted profile covers them.

open_review_findings.observation: Historical confirmed finding: A generic strict-NULL shortcut cannot implement string_to_array(text, NULL), whose delimiter NULL means character splitting; optional NULL markers also need overload-specific handling.
open_review_findings.resolution: Per-signature NULL policy plus nonempty, empty and NULL PostgreSQL probes.

open_review_findings.observation: Serialized evidence is portable. Solver cursor continuation currently requires matching compiler/parser/JAR/bridge fingerprints and replayed atom prefix; a changed native binary requires a new revision.
open_review_findings.resolution: Keep archive import/view separate from pinned-tool cursor resume; do not advertise unrestricted cross-platform continuation.

delegation.parser_and_relational: CTE materialization/demand, SRF/window composition, lock lineage and independently probed lock ownership.
delegation.formal_and_state: Lean composition contracts, sequence/rollback semantics, uniqueness/UDF integration and independent completeness review.
delegation.scalar_and_effects: Builtin NULL policies, collections/regex, notification/advisory/backend context and actual PostgreSQL oracles.
delegation.integrator: Shared interface ownership, tuple-version contract, authentic context refresh, stale evidence invalidation, combined corpus gates and deterministic Alloy/evidence serialization.

remaining_corpus_patterns.maintenance: Extend these existing modules with documented functions of at most 30 formatted lines. Retain this maintained design and reproducible evidence; do not create per-query handlers, a second evaluator or duplicate per-pass reports.

flow: Request next example or counterexample on demand
Inspect Graphviz instance and grounded AI summary
Swipe right to accept a use case or left to reject unintended behavior
Review the next agentic revision against preserved and rejected cases

triple: Exact Alloy source, assertion/run command and bounds
instance_card.graphviz: Implemented: deterministic presentation DOT derived in the frontend from typed evidence, rendered by pinned self-hosted Graphviz/WASM and sanitized. Rust-generated DOT and an equivalent server renderer remain future private-deployment options; presentation does not replace SQL semantics.
graph_semantics: Stable occurrence nodes preserve duplicate rows
Typed NULL is explicit and distinct from absent edges
Before/after tables and changed cells are distinguished
Ordered result positions, SQLSTATE and effects remain visible
Alloy atom/tuple detail can be inspected without treating atom names as business IDs
Each graph element links to a stable evidence fact reference

ai_summary.input: Versioned instance JSON plus exact SQL/IR/Alloy triple, declared business policy, schema, session context, scope and replay evidence
output: Evidence fact references for each factual claim
Why it satisfies or violates the selected property
ai_summary.trust: AI text is untrusted explanation; it cannot change solver status, hide effects or create a safety claim. Missing/failed AI leaves the graph and deterministic evidence usable.
ai_summary.privacy: BYOT OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini-compatible portal; explicit provider/context selection and redaction before sending. Provider secrets never enter instance JSON, DOT, cursor or logs.

right.meaning: Preserve this admissible observation as a positive regression case

left.meaning: Exclude this unwanted observation in the next candidate revision; infer a general rule only as an explicit reviewable proposal

feedback.persistence: Append-only versioned JSON events separate from immutable solver evidence; retry is idempotent, undo appends a superseding event, stale revision labels require explicit revalidation.
feedback.accessibility: Right/left swipe gestures have labeled Accept use case / Reject side behavior buttons, keyboard actions, screen-reader graph/table descriptions and undo.
feedback.conflicts: Contradictory live labels for the same contextual semantic observation stop automatic promotion and expose the conflicting intent.

agentic_pass.input: Prior revision plus active feedback, existing invariants and pinned industrial corpus
agentic_pass.proposal: AI may propose SQL, RA or policy edits and rationale. Deterministic binding emits a new IR/Alloy revision; old artifacts stay immutable.
required_gates: Kernel-checked Lean specification before any new semantic capability
Accepted instances remain admissible under mapped context
Rejected instances cannot be reproduced under the proposed policy/query
Actual Alloy check with independent satisfiable assumptions and exact witness replay
Fresh PostgreSQL16 industrial corpus checks, including declared contexts and expected errors
Adversarial check against overfitting one atom labeling, silently shrinking bounds, filtering counterexamples or changing domain/context to manufacture a pass
agentic_pass.promotion: Show SQL/IR/policy diff, affected accepted/rejected cases, new instances and residual bounded limitations. Swipes do not authorize running mutations on a production database or deploying changes.

security_and_portability: Escape all SQL/data labels in DOT; disable externally supplied HTML/URL/file/image attributes
Do not execute SQL strings or graph hyperlinks as instructions
Treat database values and AI summaries as untrusted content; isolate Graphviz render resources
Use portable local/private storage adapters; keep schema-versioned export/import independent of cloud/provider
No external renderer/CDN required for private deployments
acceptance_tests: Serialize/import/reopen preserves instance identity and replay evidence
Next on demand distinguishes instance/exhaustion/limit/error and cannot skip stored cursor prefix
Graph retains duplicate occurrences, typed NULLs, ordering and before/after changes
AI citations resolve only to supplied facts and unsupported claims are flagged
Repeated swipe/undo is idempotent and revision-bound
Left-swipe revision rejects unwanted behavior while retaining right-swipe use cases
Keyboard and button flow equals gesture flow
Offline/provider failure leaves visualization, review and next-instance navigation functional

delegation.formal: Check feedback/revision/completeness obligations without added axioms
delegation.rust: Evidence storage, deterministic DOT, identity/fact references, replay and feedback journal
delegation.frontend: Graphviz card, swipe/button/keyboard/undo and accessible relation tables
delegation.ai: Grounded summary contract and proposal pipeline; baseline GPT-6.1 Sol plus verified production provider availability
delegation.adversarial: Prompt/data injection, stale labels, graph omission, duplicate loss, overfitting, vacuity and solver-status conflation
